paras: The police shooting of Mary Coleman took place at Helena, Arkansas, in August 1900, when a policeman trying to arrest Coleman, a Black woman, shot her three times in the abdomen. She was reported "mortally wounded," and the brief account, which gave only the officer's version, ran in at least six Arkansas weeklies.

According to the report, the officer was attempting to arrest Coleman when she got hold of his pistol; the cause of the arrest was not given. He borrowed another pistol and pursued her, and, by his account, when he came within a few feet of her she began firing at him. He returned the fire, and she fell with three bullets in her abdomen.
The coverage does not report whether Coleman died, name the officer, or mention an inquest or any charge against him.

The item circulated as a numbered paragraph of Arkansas state news, appearing first in the Forrest City Times on August 17 and then in the Van Buren Press, the Conway Log Cabin, the Malvern Times-Journal, the Paris Express and the De Queen Bee through August 24. Each paper printed the same wording, describing Coleman as "colored" and presenting the officer's account of the struggle without attribution or another version. Most headed it "Shot by a Policeman," the Conway Log Cabin used "Officer Shoots a Woman," and the De Queen Bee's column deck read "Colored Woman Shot and Fatally Wounded While Resisting An Officer."
No coverage of the shooting was found in the Black press.
